data.title: Alpine Income Property Trust Launches $35 Million Preferred and $150 Million Common ATM Programs
data.description:

data.title: Itafos Announces Release Date for Q3 2026 Results and Business Update Webcast
data.description:
HOUSTON, Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Itafos Inc. (TSX-V: IFOS) OTCQX:ITFS (“Itafos” or “the Company”) today announces that its financial results for Q3 2026 will be released after market close on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. An on-demand recorded webcast of management commentary that reviews the Q3 2026 financial results, provides an update on the business, and addresses analysts’ and investors’ recent frequently asked questions will be available on Thursday, November 5, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. ET. The webcast will be available on the Presentations & Events page of the Company’s website www.itafos.com/investors/presentations-fact-sheets/ and will be available for 90 days.

About Itafos

The Company is a phosphate and specialty fertilizer company with businesses and projects spanning three continents:

  • Conda – a vertically integrated phosphate fertilizer business located in Idaho, US with production capacity as follows:
    • approximately 550kt per year of MAP, MAP with micronutrients (“MAP+”), superphosphoric acid (“SPA”), and merchant grade phosphoric acid (“MGA”); and
    • approximately 27kt per year of hydrofluorosilicic acid (“HFSA”);
  • Arraias – a vertically integrated phosphate fertilizer business located in Tocantins, Brazil with the following production targets (following the proposed restart of the beneficiation circuit):
    • approximately 275kt per year of SSP, PAPR and DAPR;
      • approximately 170kt per year of SSP, 60kt per year of PAPR and 45kt per year of DAPR;
    • approximately 40kt per year of excess sulfuric acid (220kt per year gross sulfuric acid production capacity);
  • Farim – a high-grade phosphate mine project located in Farim, Guinea-Bissau; and
  • Santana – a vertically integrated high-grade phosphate mine and fertilizer plant project located in Pará, Brazil.

The Company is a Delaware corporation with operations in the United States, Brazil and Guinea-Bissau. The Company’s shares trade on the TSX-V under the ticker “IFOS”. The Company’s shares also trade in the US on the OTCQX® Best Market (“OTCQX”) under the ticker symbol “ITFS”. The Company’s principal shareholder is CL Fertilizers Holding LLC, which is an affiliate of global private investment firm Castlelake, L.P.

data.title: Bitwise Dogecoin ETF Reaches Scheduled Liquidation As Holders Face Cash Redemption
data.description:
TL;DR: Bitwise’s BWOW Dogecoin ETF reached its announced October 22 liquidation distribution date, with remaining shareholders due cash based on the fund’s net asset value.

For investors who held the Bitwise Dogecoin ETF past its final day of trading, the exit is now a cash-redemption process rather than a normal market order. The fund's previously announced liquidation calendar points to October 22 for distribution of proceeds to remaining holders.

Bitwise told investors in September that BWOW would cease trading on the NYSE Arca after October 14. The sponsor subsequently planned to liquidate the portfolio and distribute the value of remaining holdings through investors' brokerage accounts, using an October 21 net asset valuation.

What happens to shares after trading stops

An ETF closing is not the same as the cryptocurrency underlying its strategy disappearing. Dogecoin continues to trade in the broader market; the BWOW product is the investment vehicle being wound down.

Shareholders who sold before the final trading deadline exited through the exchange. Those still holding shares at liquidation are due cash based on the fund's applicable net asset value, subject to normal broker processing arrangements and the terms laid out in the regulatory filing.

The SEC filing says distributions are expected on or around October 22. That wording matters: a scheduled distribution is not proof that every brokerage account has already been credited by the time an article is published.

Bitwise described the closure as part of its decision to optimize the product range. That should not be turned into an unsupported claim about the specific reasons for every investor's decision to buy or sell the fund.

Why product closures deserve attention

Crypto investment products attract headlines when they launch, especially when a fund offers convenient exposure to a popular token. The exit process is less glamorous but equally important. A sponsor needs to manage trading cutoffs, portfolio liquidation, calculation of value and communication to holders.

A security can provide exposure to a digital asset without offering the same rights as directly holding coins in a wallet. Investors therefore need to understand how a redemption is processed and whether receiving cash may create a taxable event under their circumstances.

There are also lessons for issuers. New products compete for liquidity, attention and sufficient assets to justify their ongoing operating costs. The existence of an exchange listing does not guarantee a fund will remain open indefinitely.

This week's scheduled distribution provides a concrete reminder of that lifecycle. It is a corporate-action story about one ETF, not evidence that Dogecoin itself has undergone a protocol change or lost its entire market.

Source: www.sec.gov original announcement or data.

Related Reading: crypto exchanges; Bitcoin; crypto custody.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: U.S. Dollar Advances As Concerns Of Rate Hike Due To Possible Higher Inflation Increase
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - The U.S. Dollar value edged higher on Friday as crude oil prices continued to surge for the second day supported by concerns of a potential U.S.-Iran war. Oil-driven inflation worries have led to expectations of an interest rate hike in the U.S.

Today, the U.S. Dollar Index DXY, which measures the Greenback against a basket of other major currencies, was last seen trading at 101.81, up by 0.21 (or 0.21%).

While against the Euro, the USD was trading at 1.119, up by 0.18%, against the GBP, the USD was trading at 1.337, up by 0.24%.

Against the USD, the Japanese Yen was trading at 156.831, down by 0.05%, the Swiss Franc was trading at 0.825, down by 0.60%; and the Canadian Dollar was trading at 1.401, down by 0.02%.

Against one unit of Australian Dollar, the USD was trading at 0.703, down by 0.23%.

Crude oil prices skyrocketed today adding to yesterday's surge.

Middle East tensions due to escalation in Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and reports of a possible military campaign on Iran by the U.S. continued to impact the currency market today.

The U.S.-Iran war is set to enter the ninth month by next week.

In the recent weeks, the U.S. halted its military attacks on Iran and Iran refrained from striking the U.S. bases situated in neighboring nations.

However, leaders of both nations continued to engage in exchange of verbal rhetoric.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps announced that Iran is capable of defending against any attack.

The IRGC also added that it would unveil a sophisticated weapon to combat any U.S. attack, which it termed as the 'Father Of All Bombs'.

Yesterday, the New York Times reported that the U.S. and Israel have planned for a joint military operation against Iran's nuclear installations, energy infrastructures, and missile and drone capabilities, after the U.S. mid-term elections in November.

Since the news broke out, concerns of a deep and intense conflict in the U.S. and the eventual disruption to oil and energy supply from the arab to the rest of the nations have jumped.

Oil-linked inflation threats are returning to the markets. Economists are of the view that major central banks could be forced to hike interest rates.

U.S. President Donald Trump messaged via Truth Social that Iran is cooking up stories to drive up oil prices ahead of the U.S. elections.

In an interview with Financial Times, U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz speculated that the war with Iran could last one more year but added that the Iranian regime could come to the negotiating table before that.

Today, before leaving to Florida, Trump repeated that the U.S. is in a position to end the war with Iran quickly or let the nation wither under sanctions.

Elsewhere in the Middle East, following the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's airports and other energy infrastructures, oil major Aramco instructed its staff to evacuate Dhahran headquarters.

Houthis claimed attacking Saudi Arabia's defense headquarters in Riyadh.

The U.S. Federal Reserve is slated to announce the interest rate next week.

The odds on a rate hike by the Fed were hovering at 7.20% yesterday.

Currently, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool, investors are betting on a 9.40% chance of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike at the upcoming meeting of the Fed on October 27-28 and the bets on the rates being held at the current level stand at 90.60%.

On the economic front, data released by S&P Global revealed that the composite Purchasing Managers Index in the U.S. decreased to 57.60 in October from 58.40 in September.

While the manufacturing PMI edged up to 56.00 in October from 55.90 in September, services PMI edged down to 57.9 in October 2026 from 58.8 in September.

The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index was revised higher to 48.00 in late October, up from a preliminary estimate of 46.30 but remained at its lowest level in five months.

In Japan, the annual inflation rate accelerated to 2.10% in September from 1.90% in the previous two months, marking the highest level since December 2025. On a month-on-month basis, the consumer prices showed no growth from a month earlier in September, following a 0.10% gain in the previous period.

The core consumer price index (which excludes fresh food but includes energy) increased 2.10% year-on-year in September 2026, following a 1.70% rise in August.

data.title: Colombia swaps 10.3 trillion pesos of local debt
data.description:
Colombia's Finance Ministry carried out a swap of domestic public debt securities worth 10.3 trillion pesos ($3.23 billion) on Friday to extend maturities and reduce short-term repayment pressures amid the country's fiscal challenges, the finance ministry said.

In the transaction, the government repurchased TES local government bonds maturing between November 2026 and November 2027, exchanging them for bonds maturing between 2027 and 2062, the ministry said.

The operation was the second of three local debt swaps the government plans to conduct before the end of the year.

In the previous swap, carried out in early October, the government exchanged 19.8 trillion pesos ($6.2 billion) of debt.

TES bonds are the government's second-largest source of domestic financing after tax revenue.

According to the Finance Ministry, a third debt swap is scheduled for Nov. 19.

The government of President Abelardo De La Espriella announced changes to this year's spending budget in August, including an additional 35 trillion pesos ($10.97 billion) in borrowing to cover a widening fiscal deficit forecast, which was revised up to 7.2% of gross domestic product from a previous target of 5.3%.

($1 = 3.185,01 pesos)

data.title: Stocks, Pulled in Two Directions, Fall to End Volatile Week — WSJ
data.description:
By Hannah Erin Lang

There are two major worries weighing on Wall Street these days. Both are starting to reach a fever pitch.

On one side are concerns about the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence spending boom. On the other: the ever-looming threat of rising inflation thanks in large part to persistent conflict in the Middle East.

Major U.S. indexes whipsawed this week on a grab bag of related anxieties, from soaring oil prices to outsize AI spending and the capital required to foot that bill. Those fears on Thursday sent the Nasdaq composite to one of its worst days of 2026, while on Friday Brent crude vaulted to some of its highest year-to-date levels.

The S&P 500 ended the week 0.5% lower, while the Nasdaq dropped 0.7%. The Dow industrials edged 0.4% higher on the week. On Friday, the Dow led indexes lower, falling 1.2%, or 653 points, while Nasdaq fell only 0.2%.

The week was the latest installment of a choppy trading stretch that has kept stocks more or less in place since the end of the summer, as a pivotal midterm election and the rest of the third-quarter earnings season loom.

One factor driving recent swings: investors' nerves about tech companies' huge AI-focused spending spree. Earlier this past week, positive developments at major players such as SpaceX and Anthropic juiced optimism. Traders set aside their concerns to send shares of Advanced Micro Devices, Nvidia and Tesla higher.

The tide turned on Thursday, after Meta Platforms said it would create a new class of nonvoting stock to raise the capital needed for developing and serving AI models. That left Wall Street wondering if the Facebook parent — and its peers — could secure enough capital to fund the build-out.

"More and more these [AI] infrastructure-related investments are driven by debt. At the same time you have rates rising," said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments. "That's posing some questions around 'If rates keep going higher, how much more can these companies borrow?'"

After a punishing bond rout over the past two months propelled the 10-year Treasury yield well above 5%, Thursday's tech fears sent investors fleeing for the perceived safety of government bonds. Treasury yields, which fall when prices rise, saw their biggest one-day drop in three years. The 10-year yield finished the week at 4.987%.

That was reassuring for fixed-income traders. "For a bond guy like me...it's good to see," said Vincent Ahn, president and portfolio manager at SLW Investments. "It's sort of a relief."

The declines might prove temporary. On Friday, the focus was on a different threat to stocks: global benchmark oil prices climbed back to levels last seen in April, as traders bet on renewed fighting in Iran after the election.

That put the focus back on the threat of inflation, tugging Treasury yields higher. Rising fuel costs have already scrambled interest-rate forecasts this year, eventually leading the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates for the first time in three years. Economists have warned that the longer that oil prices remain elevated, the greater the threat to the U.S. economy.

At the end of the week, those concerns were brought to the fore. Stocks in sectors that are sensitive to economic shifts, including banks and industrial firms, were among those leading losses in the S&P 500. Consumer-related stocks from Home Depot to Nike, Coca-Cola and McDonald's all fell more than 1.6% Friday.

Even as tech stocks recovered on Friday, bonds of AI-related companies continued to struggle. The extra yields, or spreads, that investors demand to hold the bonds of Oracle, SpaceX and Meta Platforms climbed again — extending their sharp gains over the past two weeks.

Investors have said there are reasons to believe that stocks can advance through the end of the year — one being the boom in third-quarter profits that American companies are expected to report in the coming weeks. Next week brings a much-awaited Fed meeting, but most traders expect central bankers to hold off on increasing rates until later meetings.

But geopolitical tensions and AI jitters are likely to weigh on share prices in the near term, Feldman said. "There's just a lot more debate about the sustainability and duration of the AI infrastructure build-out," he said. "We're going to need some more proof points as everyone gets through earnings when it comes to the return on investments."

Write to Hannah Erin Lang at hannaherin.lang@wsj.com

data.title: Tesla Stock Lags Apple Because Of ‘Communications Problem,’ Says Investor Gary Black
data.description:
Key points:
  • Black said Tesla must divulge data on how many customers keep their full self-driving (FSD) subscriptions 3-6 months after the free trial of the technology ends.
  • The comment comes on the heels of Tesla confirming earlier this week that over 75% of deliveries in North America in the third quarter included a sign-up for a paid FSD subscription at the time of delivery.
  • According to Black, the 75% is “clearly inflated.”

EV giant Tesla Inc (TSLA) has a “communications problem,” according to investor Gary Black, managing partner of The Future Fund LLC, who argued on Friday that the company’s approach undermines credibility despite technically strong products.

“I’ve said for years that TSLA’s Achilles’ heel is poor communications. $AAPL does not have a credibility problem,” Black said in a post on X, highlighting that over the past year Apple gained 33%, while Tesla fell 17%. Over five years, Apple advanced 133% while Tesla was up only 9%, he added.

Black further linked the alleged communications issue to longer-term effects, stating that Tesla stock has not moved in five years because of a lack of credibility stemming from “overpromise and hyped-up expectations.”

Black Calls TSLA’s FSD Data ‘Inflated’

Black said Tesla must divulge data on how many customers keep their full self-driving (FSD) subscriptions 3-6 months after the free trial of the technology ends, instead of immediately after the free trial period.

The comment comes on the heels of Tesla confirming earlier this week that over 75% of deliveries in North America in the third quarter included a sign-up for a paid FSD subscription at the time of delivery. According to Black, the 75% is “clearly inflated.” RBC Capital analyst Tom Narayan previously pegged FSD attach rate at 30-40% on a paid basis.

Black’s Consistent Critique Of TSLA Communications

Black’s Friday comments continue a consistent critique. He has previously argued that Tesla has not acted like a market leader by educating non-EV owners on benefits such as convenience, lower costs, performance, and technology, and has instead leaned on discounts or price cuts.

He has also called for a more proactive public relations strategy, noting that journalists often cite Tesla’s lack of engagement and that the media will run one-sided stories without company-provided context. Ahead of past earnings periods, Black has urged Tesla leadership to improve credibility by avoiding outlandish promises and bringing in experienced communications support. In other posts, he has warned that allowing products to speak for themselves risks wasting advantages in the vehicle autonomy race.

Meanwhile, Tesla Seeks EU, China Approval Of FSD

Earlier this week, during Tesla’s third-quarter earnings call, CEO Elon Musk pegged FSD as a key demand driver and expressed optimism for approval of the technology across the EU within a few months as part of a push for approval across markets. The company also said that it is looking forward to approval for the technology in China.

As per the company, there are over 1.7 million paid customers for FSD globally. The technology automates several aspects of driving but is yet to enable fully autonomous driving in customer-owned vehicles.

How Did TSLA Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TSLA stock fell from 'bullish' to 'bearish' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at 'high' levels.

TSLA stock has dropped 17% year-to-date.

data.title: Earnings flood, Fed meeting will test rickety AI market rally
data.description:
Key points:
  • AI trade in focus with hyperscaler results: Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon
  • Fed rate decision due on Wednesday, with markets expecting pause after Sept hike
  • Big Q3 earnings week also includes Intel, Sandisk, Lilly, Caterpillar

By Lewis Krauskopf

US stock investors face a pivotal week, with corporate earnings reports led by major AI players and a Federal Reserve meeting posing critical tests for a suddenly shaky market rally.

Weakness in technology shares left investors on edge about the state of the AI trade that has driven the US equity bull market that just marked its fourth anniversary.

The Nasdaq Composite posted a slim loss on Friday, a day after the tech-heavy index suffered its biggest daily drop since June. Investors were disappointed by quarterly reports from Meta and Lam Research . Meta is one of the hyperscalers spending massively to build out data centers, while Lam is a high-flying semiconductor company, one of a group that has been among the biggest AI stock winners.

Three other hyperscalers — Alphabet , Microsoft and Amazon — headline a packed week of quarterly results, including about one-third of S&P 500 companies. The Fed's interest rate policy meeting on Wednesday also could rattle markets.

"There are a lot of balls in the air," said Nick Giorgi, chief equity strategist at Alpine Macro.

"Next week, you have a lot more tech earnings, and right now the market is taking a discerning eye as it relates to all the spending that goes along with artificial intelligence," Giorgi said. "The market's just not giving the benefit of the doubt to companies that are spending a ton of money on building this all out, which to us is actually very healthy, but still does augur for some short-term pain."

Investors also have their focus trained on the US midterm elections on November 3, with growing bets that the Democrats will wrest control of the US Congress away from President Donald Trump's Republican party. The series of market catalysts could ratchet up volatility over the next couple of weeks and challenge optimism that has helped lift the benchmark S&P 500 index CBOE:SPX up 11% in 2026.

HYPERSCALERS ON THE HOT SEAT

Robust US profit growth has underpinned the stock market's gains this year in the face of headwinds including spiking Treasury yields and rising energy costs stemming from the Middle East conflict.

With more than 100 companies having posted results so far, third-quarter S&P 500 earnings are on pace to have climbed more than 32% from a year ago, according to LSEG IBES data. Next week is the busiest of the reporting season.

"I think earnings will determine whether this ... tech pullback is a buying opportunity, or is there a deeper correction ahead," said King Lip, chief strategist at BakerAvenue Wealth Management. "What we need is just another round of really strong earnings."

Alphabet and Microsoft report on Wednesday. Amazon's results are due Thursday. Focus will be on the guidance the companies give on capital spending plans and whether they are seeing returns on the massive outlays.

Capital spending from hyperscalers, expected to be around $800 billion this year, is boosting the bottom lines for a wide swath of companies involved in the AI buildout. But investors are wary of the sustainability of such spending amid mounting financing costs.

"Earnings are critical to the overall confidence level of the AI trade and how much longer the spend will continue," said Kevin Mahn, president and chief investment officer at Hennion & Walsh Asset Management.

FED EXPECTED TO PAUSE ON RATES, FOR NOW

Quarterly reports next week from chip companies Intel and Sandisk also could influence the AI trade.

Elsewhere, other high-profile companies set to report next week include drugmaker Eli Lilly , oil majors Exxon and Chevron and industrial equipment giant Caterpillar .

The prospect for more interest rate hikes also comes into focus with the Fed meeting. The Fed raised rates in September for the first time since 2023, in an effort to control above-target inflation, but Fed funds futures late on Friday suggested a less-than 10% chance the Fed will hike again when it gives its policy statement on Wednesday, according to LSEG data.

One factor: Investors are dubious that the Fed will want to increase rates just a week before the midterm elections.

However, markets are leaning toward a hike at the next meeting in December, with futures suggesting a roughly 80% probability of such a move then.

Walter Todd, chief investment officer at Greenwood Capital, said he will be watching for any hints about the rate path at Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference following the decision.

"Does he say something to give an idea about December, because right now the expectation is there is going to be a hike," Todd said.
